You are doing a pre-production security review of a large, already-built feature in the git worktree /opt/nxeon-wip-staff-platform (branch feature/staff-platform, off the Nxeon production repo at /opt/nxeon). This is about to be merged to main and deployed to production, so treat this as a real, adversarial code review — the goal is to find anything that would let an EMPLOYEE-role user (a genuinely limited-access hire) reach more than they should, or let ANY user bypass the new IP-whitelist/RBAC controls.

Read the full plan first for context: /root/.claude/plans/validated-napping-possum.md.

I've already personally verified these specific things are correct, so don't re-verify them, just be aware they're solid:
- `app/staff/clients/page.tsx`'s Prisma query — confirmed it selects ONLY id/name/email/createdAt/_count(tickets,servers), nothing sensitive.
- `lib/firewall-rules.ts`'s `ipInCidr()` — tested against 8 real/edge cases (exact match, CIDR ranges, malformed CIDR, /0, /33, garbage input), all correct.
- `lib/staff-ip.ts`'s `staffIpBlocked()` — fail-open with zero rows, fail-closed per-user once rows exist, correct trusted-IP-header extraction.
- `app/staff/layout.tsx` — host gate, role gate (EMPLOYEE + ADMIN only), impersonation refusal, dynamic nav-from-grants, all read and confirmed correct.

## What I need YOU to check (things I haven't verified yet)

1. **Every single gate migration from Phase 2** — re-derive this yourself by reading the actual current code, don't trust any prior summary: `lib/actions-reddit-templates.ts`, `lib/actions-company-mail.ts`, `lib/mail/imap.ts`'s `resolveMailbox`, `lib/actions-support.ts`'s `requireTicketActor`, `lib/actions-chat.ts`. For EACH exported/relevant function, confirm the gate is exactly as strict as it should be — no function that should require `companyMailboxes` specifically was accidentally left on the broader `companyInbox` OR-check, no function that touches money/billing/impersonation slipped through with just an area/grant check when it should require full `requireAdmin()`.

2. **`lib/actions-staff.ts`** — this is the file that GRANTS access to everything else. Confirm `createEmployee`, `setStaffGrant`, `addStaffIp`, `removeStaffIp` are ALL gated `requireAdmin()` specifically (imported from `@/lib/auth`), never `requireGrant`/`requireAreaOrGrant` from `lib/staff-grants.ts` — if any of these were accidentally gated with the grant-based helpers instead of a hard ADMIN check, an EMPLOYEE could theoretically grant themselves (or another employee) more access. Also confirm `setStaffGrant` actually validates that its target user has `role === "EMPLOYEE"` before writing a grant (so an admin fat-fingering a customer's user id can't accidentally grant them staff tool access).

3. **The six wired-in staff routes from Phase 5** (`app/staff/{support,support/[id],chat,reddit,inbox,mailboxes}/page.tsx`) — confirm each one's `requireAreaOrGrant(...)` call uses the CORRECT area matching its actual content (e.g. `/staff/mailboxes` must require `companyMailboxes`, not the broader `companyInbox`). Also check the shared components they render (`components/admin/SupportDeskView.tsx`, `SupportTicketView.tsx`, `ChatDeskView.tsx`, `CompanyInboxView.tsx`) for any leftover ADMIN-only action button (impersonate, suspend, credit, delete-everything) that might render in a context now also reachable by a granted EMPLOYEE — these components are shared between `/admin` and `/staff`, so anything ADMIN-only rendered inside them needs its own internal `user.role === "ADMIN"` check, not just being reachable via an ADMIN-only PAGE like before.

4. **`components/support/CannedReplyPicker.tsx` and `lib/actions-canned-replies.ts`** — confirm the delete action truly requires ADMIN (per the plan, this was a deliberate judgment call) and that create/edit/list are gated to `supportTickets`/`liveChat` grant-holders, not open to any authenticated user.

5. **The task system (`lib/actions-work.ts`, `app/api/work/attachments/**`)** — confirm EVERY exported action is gated `requireGrant("tasks")`/`requireAreaOrGrant("tasks")` with no exceptions, and specifically check the attachment upload/download routes for a path-traversal risk in how `storedName`/`taskId` are used to construct filesystem paths (this is a common vulnerability class in file-upload features — confirm filenames are sanitized/generated server-side, never taken verbatim from user input for the actual disk path).

6. **Structural regressions**: run `DATABASE_URL="postgresql://user:pass@localhost:5432/dummy" npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` and `DATABASE_URL="postgresql://user:pass@localhost:5432/dummy" npm test` yourself, fresh, right now (the worktree has had many rounds of edits since it was last tested by anyone) — confirm tsc is still clean and confirm the test failure count is still exactly the 37 pre-existing failures unrelated to this work (list them if it's different from 37, and investigate any NEW failure since the last check, since new agents may have touched files after the count was last confirmed).

7. **Full diff sanity scan**: run `git -C /opt/nxeon-wip-staff-platform diff --stat main` and `git -C /opt/nxeon-wip-staff-platform status` and look for anything unexpected — a file touched that has no business being touched by this feature, an accidentally-committed secret, a stray console.log with sensitive data, a debug bypass left in (e.g. a hardcoded `if (true)` or a commented-out auth check).

## Report format

Report a clear PASS/FAIL verdict for each of the 7 areas above, with exact file:line citations for anything you find. If you find a real issue, describe exactly what's wrong and what the fix should be — but do NOT fix anything yourself, this is a review-only pass; I'll decide what to do with your findings before this goes to production. Be genuinely adversarial — assume there's a real bug hiding somewhere in a plan this large built across 5 parallel agents, and try hard to find it rather than rubber-stamping.

1	# Nxeon staff platform — roles, employee portal, and a project/task system
2	
3	## Context
4	
5	Nxeon just hired its first employee (marketing + customer support). Today the codebase has no way to give one specific person a hand-picked subset of admin tools — access is all-or-nothing per role (`CUSTOMER | SUPPORT | BILLING | ADMIN`), and almost everything outside billing/fleet/support is bucketed into one ADMIN-only `"platform"` area (Reddit templates, the company inbox, mailboxes, settings, staff, audit log, and more all share that one gate). The owner wants: a dedicated portal for employees (separate from both the customer dashboard and the full `/admin` ops portal), the ability to hand-pick exactly which tools each individual employee can use, a per-employee IP whitelist, and a real internal project/task-management system ("a ClickUp alternative") usable by staff with full admin oversight of everything they do. This is production work (`/opt/nxeon`) — a mistake here risks over-exposing customer data to a new hire, so it's built additively, tested on staging, and verified with a real test employee account before every promotion to prod.
6	
7	For the first employee specifically, the owner wants: Support tickets, Live chat, the Reddit template library, the company Inbox, company Mailboxes, and a new limited (name/email/signup date/ticket count/server count only) Clients view — plus a snippet library for quick replies in tickets/chat, which doesn't exist today and is being added alongside.
8	
9	## Key decisions (confirmed with the owner)
10	
11	- **Separate, dedicated employee portal** (own nav/shell), not a permission-filtered view of `/admin`.
12	- **Per-employee custom grants**, not fixed named roles — the owner checks off exactly which tools each individual hire gets.
13	- **New minimal Clients view** for limited access — no financials, no IP/location history, no audit trail, no impersonate. Just name/email/signup date/ticket count/server count.
14	- **"Mailboxes" = company mailboxes** (admin@/support@-style), paired with the company Inbox — not customer email hosting.
15	- **Live chat + a quick-replies snippet library are in scope for this pass** (my recommendation, since they're core to a support hire's job); a knowledge-base/handbook view is an explicit fast-follow, not built now — needs a first look at the existing `kb.ts`/`kb-llm.ts`/`/admin/docs` code to see what's actually reusable before committing to an approach.
16	
17	## Ground truth confirmed this session (verified directly against the code, not just recalled)
18	
19	- `lib/rbac.ts`: `Area` union has exactly 8 values (`overview, analytics, clients, support, fleet, billing, accounting, platform`), a static `AREA_ROLES: Record<Area, Role[]>` map, `canAccess(role, area)`, `isStaff(role)` (`SUPPORT|BILLING|ADMIN`), `HREF_AREA` (route → area, defaults to `"platform"`), `requireArea(area)` (redirect-based page guard, `/login` if signed out, `/dashboard` if not staff, `/admin` if wrong area). Used at ~85 admin pages and ~30 action files, often re-checked per action as defense in depth.
20	- `platform` is a genuine ADMIN-only catch-all shared by 14+ unrelated action files (ads, agency, SEO, cold-email, broadcast, staff, audit, reddit, mail, mailboxes, …) — confirmed via grep. It must not be restructured wholesale; new narrow areas get carved out instead, leaving `platform`'s other ~25 routes untouched.
21	- `support` (the existing area) is shared by far more than the ticket queue: live chat (`lib/actions-chat.ts`, 12 confirmed `requireArea("support")` call sites), the Discord support bridge, feedback, two unread-count API routes, and a structural test (`test/discord-oauth-guards.test.ts`) that hardcodes the literal string `requireArea("support")`. Renaming/splitting `support` itself is out — new narrow areas (`supportTickets`, `liveChat`) are added alongside it instead, and only the ticket/chat call sites migrate to them.
22	- `lib/actions-support.ts:50-52` — confirmed by direct read: `requireTicketActor()` returns `{ id: user.id, isSupportStaff: canAccess(user.role, "support") }`, and this same helper is used for BOTH staff and customers viewing their own ticket (`ticketOwner.userId !== user.id && !user.isSupportStaff`). This is the single line that governs staff-vs-customer ticket permissions — one clean edit point.
23	- `lib/mail/imap.ts:278-285` — confirmed by direct read: `resolveMailbox()`'s staff branch is gated `if (isStaff(user.role))`, synthesizing company-mailbox access with no area check at all today. This is the REAL authority every mail action (`listFolders`/`listMessages`/`sendMessage`/etc. in `lib/actions-mail.ts`) goes through — the company-Inbox grant must reach this function, not just the page, or it repeats the exact mistake `lib/team-guard.ts` made (nav-visible, not server-enforced) before it was deliberately deleted for that reason.
24	- `lib/actions-reddit-templates.ts` — every export calls `requireAdmin()` directly (bypasses the area system entirely) — confirmed pattern, needs its own migration, not just the page's gate.
25	- `lib/actions-company-mail.ts` — every export calls `requireArea("platform")` — confirmed.
26	- `app/admin/layout.tsx:9-15` (`adminHostBlocked`, reads `NXEON_ADMIN_HOSTS`, 404s on host mismatch, fails open if unset) and `:30-56` (`adminIpBlocked`, reads the `allowed_admin_ips` setting, trusts `x-real-ip`/last `x-forwarded-for` hop, fails open on empty/malformed list or undeterminable IP) — both read in full. This is the exact scaffolding to copy for a third, separately-hosted employee portal and its own per-employee IP gate.
27	- `lib/firewall-rules.ts:70` has `normalizeCidr()` already (validates/normalizes a CIDR for storage) — reusable for the new per-employee IP list, though a runtime `ipInCidr(ip, cidr)` matcher doesn't exist yet and needs adding.

32	## Phase 1 — Data model (additive only)
33	
34	`prisma/schema.prisma` changes, all nullable/new, safe to `db push` ahead of any code that reads them:
35	
36	- `enum Role`: add `EMPLOYEE` (deliberately not `STAFF` — `isStaff()` already means `SUPPORT|BILLING|ADMIN` in ~8 files; a same-named role would silently read as included when it isn't).
37	- `StaffGrant { id, userId (FK→User, cascade), area (String, validated against the Area union in code — matches this schema's existing convention of plain strings for fast-changing value sets), createdById?, createdAt }`, `@@unique([userId, area])`.
38	- `StaffIpAllow { id, userId (FK, cascade), cidr (String, normalized via normalizeCidr at write time), label?, createdAt }` — a list of rows per user (not a comma-string like the global setting), since per-user add/remove is a first-class UI action here.
39	- `CannedReply { id, title, body, createdById (FK→User), createdAt, updatedAt }` — the new quick-replies snippet library, usable from both tickets and live chat.
40	- Task-system models, prefixed `Work*` so they can never be confused with or wired into the dev-ops `Card`/`Board` tables: `WorkBoard { id, name, description?, archivedAt?, createdById, createdAt }`, `WorkColumn { id, boardId (FK, cascade), name, position }`, `WorkTask { id, boardId (FK, cascade), columnId (FK, cascade), title, description (default ""), priority (reuse existing CardPriority enum), assigneeId? (real FK→User, onDelete SetNull), dueAt?, position, archivedAt?, completedAt?, createdById, createdAt, updatedAt }`, `WorkChecklistItem { id, taskId (FK, cascade), label, done (default false), position, createdAt }`, `WorkTaskComment { id, taskId (FK, cascade), authorId (real FK→User), body, createdAt }`, `WorkTaskAttachment { id, taskId (FK, cascade), filename, storedName, mime, sizeBytes, kind (reuse AttachmentKind enum), uploadedById, createdAt }`. Indexes on every FK, plus `@@index([assigneeId])` on `WorkTask` for "my tasks" queries. No per-board membership/ACL table yet (MVP: any `tasks`-granted user sees every board) — noted as a future idea, not built now.
41	
42	Run `npm run db:push` (staging DB first) + `npx prisma generate` once this phase lands, before any Phase 2+ code depends on it.
43	
44	## Phase 2 — RBAC gating primitive + migrating existing gates
45	
46	New file `lib/staff-grants.ts` (kept separate from `lib/rbac.ts` so its ~115 existing call sites are provably untouched):
47	- `hasAreaAccess(user, area)` — `canAccess(user.role, area)` fast path (unchanged for CUSTOMER/SUPPORT/BILLING/ADMIN, no DB hit); only `EMPLOYEE` falls through to a `StaffGrant` lookup.
48	- `hasAnyAreaAccess(user, areas[])` — OR logic (needed since company-mailbox listing is reachable from either the Inbox or Mailboxes grant).
49	- `requireGrant(area)` / `requireAnyGrant(areas[])` — throwing variants for server actions.
50	- `requireAreaOrGrant(area)` — redirecting variant, drop-in shape-compatible with `requireArea` for page files.
51	- `listGrantedAreas(userId)` — feeds the employee portal's dynamic nav and the admin grant-checklist UI.
52	
53	`lib/rbac.ts` additions (small, additive, no existing entries touched): extend `Area` with `redditTemplates | companyInbox | companyMailboxes | clientsBasic | supportTickets | liveChat | tasks`; extend `AREA_ROLES` with each (TypeScript's `Record<Area,Role[]>` forces completeness) — `supportTickets`/`liveChat` get `["SUPPORT","ADMIN"]` (identical to today's `support`, so legacy behavior for existing staff is unchanged), `tasks` gets `["SUPPORT","BILLING","ADMIN"]`, the rest get `["ADMIN"]`; extend `HREF_AREA` for `/admin/reddit`, `/admin/inbox`, `/admin/mailboxes`, `/admin/support` (→ `supportTickets`), `/admin/chat` (→ `liveChat`), plus new `/admin/clients-basic` and `/admin/tasks` entries. Every other `platform`/`support` mapping is left exactly as-is.
54	
55	Action-file migrations (mechanical, each verified against the real code above):
56	- `lib/actions-reddit-templates.ts`: `requireAdmin()` → `requireGrant("redditTemplates")` at every export.
57	- `lib/actions-company-mail.ts`: list functions → `requireAnyGrant(["companyInbox","companyMailboxes"])`; CRUD/credential-reveal functions → `requireGrant("companyMailboxes")` (kept stricter than plain listing).
58	- `lib/mail/imap.ts`'s `resolveMailbox`: additive condition — `if (isStaff(user.role) || (user.role === "EMPLOYEE" && await hasAreaAccess(user, "companyInbox")))` — zero change for existing staff, closes the real "page-gated but data-layer-open" gap for the new role.
59	- `lib/actions-support.ts`'s `requireTicketActor()`: `isSupportStaff: canAccess(user.role, "support")` → `isSupportStaff: await hasAreaAccess(user, "supportTickets")` — this one line threads correctly into `replyTicket`/`setTicketStatus`/`writeTicketReply`, which already take the boolean as a parameter.
60	- `lib/actions-chat.ts`: all 12 `requireArea("support")` call sites → `requireAreaOrGrant`/`requireGrant("liveChat")` as appropriate (page-load vs. action).
61	- Page files (`app/admin/{reddit,inbox,mailboxes,support,support/[id],chat}/page.tsx`): swap their gate call to the new `requireAreaOrGrant(...)`.
62	
63	Structural tests to update in the same phase (or CI correctly fails): `test/company-mailbox.test.ts` (new gate patterns, `"/admin/mailboxes"` area string), `test/admin-actions-guards.test.ts` (add `requireGrant(`/`requireAnyGrant(`/`requireAreaOrGrant(` to the marker lists; add `actions-reddit-templates.ts`/`actions-company-mail.ts` to `ADMIN_ACTION_FILES`), `test/customer-actions-guards.test.ts` (update the doc-comment describing `requireTicketActor`'s derivation), `test/discord-oauth-guards.test.ts` (confirm it still passes unmodified — `support` itself isn't touched). Run `npm test` after this phase as the cheapest regression check.
64	
65	## Phase 3 — Admin "Staff" management UI (`/admin/staff`, ADMIN-only, forever)
66	
67	The route already exists (a simple role-promotion table) and is already reserved under `platform` in `lib/admin-groups.ts` — stays `requireArea("platform")`, i.e. never manageable by anyone but ADMIN, per the explicit requirement.
68	
69	Extend `app/admin/staff/page.tsx` (+ new `app/admin/staff/[id]/page.tsx` detail, mirroring the existing `/admin/users` + `[id]` split):
70	- **Create employee** — new `createEmployee(email, name, tempPassword)` action in `lib/actions-staff.ts`, `Role.EMPLOYEE`.
71	- **Grant checklist** — one checkbox per grantable area, driven by a single exported `GRANTABLE_AREAS: {area, label, hint?}[]` list (so adding a future grantable tool is a one-line addition). New `setStaffGrant(userId, area, granted)`, `requireAdmin()`-gated.
72	- **IP whitelist config** — add/remove-row UI, `addStaffIp(userId, cidr, label?)` / `removeStaffIp(userId, id)`, validated through `normalizeCidr`, `requireAdmin()`-gated.
73	- **Per-employee activity link** — jumps into the Phase 7 audit viewer pre-filtered to that employee.
74	- **Quick-replies management** — since this ships alongside, fold `CannedReply` CRUD into this same staff-management surface (or a small `/admin/canned-replies` page) so the owner can seed starter replies; employees granted `supportTickets`/`liveChat` can also create their own (they're the ones using them day to day).
75	
76	New components: `components/admin/StaffGrantChecklist.tsx`, `components/admin/StaffIpAllowlist.tsx`.
77	
78	## Phase 4 — Employee portal shell (`/staff`, new dedicated host)
79	
80	New `app/staff/layout.tsx`, mirroring `app/admin/layout.tsx`'s already-proven shape:
81	- `staffHostBlocked()` — identical logic to `adminHostBlocked()`, new env var `NXEON_STAFF_HOSTS`, fails open if unset.
82	- Auth: `realUser()`; redirect anything that isn't `EMPLOYEE` or `ADMIN` to `/dashboard` (SUPPORT/BILLING/CUSTOMER routing is completely unaffected). Let `ADMIN` in too, so the owner can log into the employee portal and see exactly what a given grant set looks like before handing it out. Refuse impersonation, same as the admin layout.
83	- **Per-employee IP enforcement** — new `lib/staff-ip.ts`, a `staffIpBlocked(userId)` structurally parallel to `adminIpBlocked()` but scoped to that user's `StaffIpAllow` rows; extract the shared `isPlainIp`-style header-trust logic into a small reusable helper so it isn't duplicated between the two gates; add a small new `ipInCidr(ip, cidr)` matcher next to the existing `normalizeCidr`. **Fail-open when zero rows exist for that employee** (avoids locking out a brand-new hire before IP config happens), **fail-closed the moment even one row exists** for that specific employee — every other employee with no rows is unaffected.
84	- **Dynamic nav** — `listGrantedAreas(user.id)` drives the nav via the same `GRANTABLE_AREAS` list from Phase 3, using the existing generic `Shell` component with a new `tag="staff"`. An employee with only two grants sees exactly two nav entries — never hardcoded.
85	- Reuse the existing `enforce_staff_2fa` setting check verbatim.
86	- Redirect targets: extend the existing `ADMIN ? "/admin" : "/dashboard"` ternary (in `lib/actions.ts` and `app/login/page.tsx`) into a tiny shared `roleHome(role)` helper — `EMPLOYEE → /staff`, everyone else unchanged.
87	
88	## Phase 5 — Wire the six granted tools into the employee portal
89	
90	For each existing tool, extract its page body into a shared, chrome-agnostic component reused by both `/admin/...` (gate swapped in Phase 2, behavior otherwise unchanged) and the new `/staff/...` route: Support tickets (`components/admin/SupportDeskView.tsx`), Live chat (reuse whatever chat UI component already exists), Reddit templates (already thin — a light duplicate or shared wrapper), company Inbox (`components/admin/CompanyInboxView.tsx`), company Mailboxes (reuse `components/admin/CompanyMailboxes.tsx` directly).
91	
92	The **new minimal Clients view** is built fresh, not extracted — this is the single most security-critical file in the whole plan: `app/staff/clients/page.tsx` (`requireAreaOrGrant("clientsBasic")`) queries with a `select` of **only** `id, name, email, createdAt` plus `_count` on `tickets`/`servers` (both confirmed-existing relations) — no balance, no transactions, no IP history, no audit relation, no notes, no impersonate rendered anywhere. A thin ADMIN-only preview at `app/admin/clients-basic/page.tsx` reusing the identical component lets the owner see exactly what an employee would see before granting it.
93	
94	Quick replies: a shared `<CannedReplyPicker>` component wired into both the ticket `ReplyForm` and the live-chat reply input, backed by simple CRUD in `lib/actions-staff.ts` (or a new small `lib/actions-canned-replies.ts`), gated by the same `supportTickets`/`liveChat` grants.
95	
96	## Phase 6 — The "ClickUp alternative" task system
97	
98	MVP: boards → columns (Kanban) → tasks, real `assigneeId` FK, due dates, priority (reused `CardPriority`), checklist sub-items, comments with real `authorId`, file attachments (same on-disk-plus-metadata pattern as the dev-ops board, separate upload directory). Adopt `dnd-kit` (small, no existing DnD library, worth it now that there will be two Kanban UIs rather than copy-pasting the hand-rolled HTML5 drag code a second time). Routes: `/admin/tasks` (`requireAreaOrGrant("tasks")`) and `/staff/tasks`, sharing `components/work/WorkBoardsView.tsx` / `WorkBoardClient.tsx`. New `lib/actions-work.ts`, every export gated + calling the shared audit helper (Phase 7) for create/move/assign/prioritize/due-date/complete/archive/checklist-toggle/comment/attachment. Notifications reuse the existing generic `Notification` model — no new model needed. Admin oversight: an Activity tab on `/admin/tasks` that's the Phase-7 audit viewer pre-filtered to `task.*` actions, with lightweight polling (mirroring the existing `AdminChatNotifier` pattern) rather than websockets.
99	
100	Hard separation from the dev-ops board: `lib/actions-work.ts` never imports `lib/actions-board.ts`; nothing in the task system can reach `runCardStageAction` or the deploy scripts it triggers.
101	
102	**Future ideas (explicitly out of MVP — answering "what else belongs here")**: recurring tasks, time tracking/estimates, a calendar/timeline (Gantt-lite) view over due dates, task templates (e.g. "new employee onboarding," "weekly Reddit round"), personal to-do lists distinct from team boards, workload/velocity dashboards sourced from the audit trail, saved filters/views, @mentions resolving to notifications, per-board membership once boards need real restriction.
103	
104	## Phase 7 — Comprehensive staff activity visibility
105	
106	New `lib/audit.ts` exporting `recordAudit(userId, action, detail?)` — a pure extraction of today's private `audit()` in `lib/actions.ts` (same body, same impersonation-attribution logic), with `lib/actions.ts` keeping a one-line alias so its 19 internal call sites don't need renaming. Every new/migrated staff-reachable action (task mutations, staff grant/IP changes, and — as a natural follow-on — the reddit/mailbox actions touched in Phase 2) imports and calls this shared helper, so employee activity is captured with the same consistency as everything else going forward. `/admin/audit` gains a "staff member" filter (`?staff=<userId>`, a straightforward `where: { userId }` addition) and a quick way to view `task.*`/`staff.*` actions — directly answers "show me everything employee X did." No change needed to impersonation-attribution logic, since `EMPLOYEE` can never impersonate (hard-gated to `ADMIN` already in `lib/auth.ts`).
107	
108	## Fast-follow (not this pass)
109	
110	Knowledge-base/handbook view for staff — first needs a look at the existing `kb.ts`/`kb-llm.ts`/`kb-tools.ts`/`kb-run.ts` files (likely backing an AI support-bot's retrieval, not a human-browsable doc library) and the `/admin/docs` internal documentation system, to see what's genuinely reusable before designing anything new.
111	
112	## Sequencing & risk notes
113	
114	Phase 3 only needs Phases 1–2, not Phase 4 — the owner can create the employee and check off grants before the portal itself exists, a reasonable early checkpoint. Phase 6 (tasks) only depends on Phase 1 + Phase 2's `requireAreaOrGrant`, so it can proceed in parallel with Phases 3–5. Phase 2 is the highest-risk phase, since it edits already-shipped, already-tested gates (`resolveMailbox`, `requireTicketActor`, the 12 chat actions) rather than only adding new code — build and test it on staging, run `npm test`, and manually verify with a real `EMPLOYEE` test account (grant exactly the intended tools, confirm everything else 403s/redirects, confirm the rest of `/admin` is untouched) before every `promote-production.sh` run from Phase 2 onward.
115	
116	## Critical files
117	
118	- `lib/rbac.ts` — `Area`/`AREA_ROLES`/`HREF_AREA` extensions (Phase 2)
119	- `lib/staff-grants.ts` (new) — `requireGrant`/`requireAnyGrant`/`requireAreaOrGrant`/`hasAreaAccess`/`listGrantedAreas` (Phase 2)
120	- `prisma/schema.prisma` — `Role.EMPLOYEE`, `StaffGrant`, `StaffIpAllow`, `CannedReply`, `Work*` models (Phase 1)
121	- `lib/mail/imap.ts` (`resolveMailbox`) and `lib/actions-support.ts` (`requireTicketActor`) and `lib/actions-chat.ts` — the real data-layer authorities that must become grant-aware, not just their pages (Phase 2)
122	- `app/staff/layout.tsx` (new) — host gate, per-employee IP enforcement, dynamic grant-driven nav (Phase 4)
123	- `app/admin/staff/page.tsx` + `lib/actions-staff.ts` — employee creation, grants, IP whitelist, ADMIN-only (Phase 3)
124	- `app/staff/clients/page.tsx` + its `select`-limited query — the single most security-critical file (Phase 5)
125	- `lib/audit.ts` (new) — shared exported audit helper (Phase 7)
126	
127	## Verification
128	
129	- Phase 2 onward: `npm test` after every gate migration (the structural RBAC tests are designed to catch exactly this class of regression).
130	- Manual QA on staging with a real `Role.EMPLOYEE` test account before each production promotion: log in, confirm the nav shows only granted tools, confirm ungranted tools 403/redirect from both the page AND a direct action call (not just hidden nav), confirm existing ADMIN/SUPPORT/BILLING behavior is byte-identical to before.
131	- IP whitelist: verify fail-open with zero rows, fail-closed the moment one row is added, from an IP both inside and outside the configured range.
132	- Task system: verify a task created/moved/commented by the test employee shows up correctly in the admin audit filter and the `/admin/tasks` activity tab.

## Security review — `/opt/nxeon-wip-staff-platform` (`feature/staff-platform`)

### 1. Phase 2 gate migrations — **PASS**
Re-derived every gate from the current code, not summaries.
- `lib/actions-reddit-templates.ts` — all 12 exports call `requireGrant("redditTemplates")`.
- `lib/actions-company-mail.ts` — listing (`listCompanyMailboxes`, `listCompanyMailboxInfos`) correctly use `requireAnyGrant(["companyInbox","companyMailboxes"])`; CRUD/reveal/reset/delete (`createCompanyMailbox`, `createDefaultCompanyMailboxes`, `revealCompanyMailboxPassword`, `resetCompanyMailboxPassword`, `deleteCompanyMailbox`) correctly use the stricter `requireGrant("companyMailboxes")` alone. No function that touches credentials slipped onto the broader OR-check.
- `lib/mail/imap.ts:291` — `resolveMailbox`'s branch is `if (isStaff(user.role) || (user.role === "EMPLOYEE" && (await hasAreaAccess(user, "companyInbox"))))` — additive, correct, matches the plan exactly.
- `lib/actions-support.ts:50-52` — `requireTicketActor()` now derives `isSupportStaff` from `hasAreaAccess(user, "supportTickets")`, threading correctly into `replyTicket`/`setTicketStatus`/`setTicketPriority`.
- `lib/actions-chat.ts` — confirmed 10/10 exports gated `requireGrant("liveChat")`, zero leftover `requireArea("support")` call sites.
- Also found (not in the checklist but correctly migrated as part of the same phase): `app/api/reddit/image/route.ts` and `app/api/reddit/image/[id]/route.ts`, previously `requireAdmin()`-only, now `requireGrant("redditTemplates")` — good catch by whoever built this, these raw upload/serve routes sit outside the action file and would otherwise 403 a granted EMPLOYEE.

### 2. `lib/actions-staff.ts` — **PASS**
`createEmployee`, `setStaffGrant`, `addStaffIp`, `removeStaffIp` (and `setUserRole`) all call `requireAdmin()` imported from `./auth` (confirmed `lib/auth.ts:229`, hard `role !== "ADMIN"` check) — never the grant-based helpers. `setStaffGrant` (line 120) refuses non-EMPLOYEE targets: `if (target.role !== "EMPLOYEE") return { error: ... }`. `addStaffIp` (line 155) has the identical check. `app/admin/staff/[id]/page.tsx` is also hard `requireArea("platform")`, never `requireAreaOrGrant`, so the grant-management UI itself can never become delegable.

### 3. Six staff routes + shared components — **FAIL (one real finding)**
All six routes gate on exactly the correct area (`/staff/mailboxes` → `companyMailboxes`, not `companyInbox`; `/staff/support` and `/staff/support/[id]` → `supportTickets`; `/staff/chat` → `liveChat`; `/staff/inbox` → `companyInbox`; `/staff/reddit` → `redditTemplates`) — same as their `/admin` counterparts. `ChatDeskView`/`ChatInbox` and `CompanyInboxView` have no ADMIN-only buttons or hidden props; every action they call is itself grant-gated.

**Real finding:** `components/admin/SupportTicketView.tsx` — shared verbatim between `/admin/support/[id]` and `/staff/support/[id]`, gated only by `requireAreaOrGrant("supportTickets")` with no internal role check — queries and renders the customer's **wallet balance** unconditionally:
- Query: line 45, `balanceCents: true` selected on `ticket.user`.
- Render: line 164, `<dd>{fmtMoney(ticket.user.balanceCents)}</dd>` in the "Customer" side panel, plus a `suspended` badge (lines 147-151).

This means an EMPLOYEE granted only `supportTickets` — one of the exact six tools the owner is handing to the first hire — sees every ticket-opener's wallet balance. The plan's explicit design intent was that the new limited-access role gets "no financials" (stated for the Clients view); this pre-existing admin/support component was extracted for dual-portal reuse without stripping that field for the EMPLOYEE case. It's not an ADMIN-only *button* (which the review specifically asked about) but the same underlying bug class: financial data now reachable by a granted EMPLOYEE with no internal `role === "ADMIN"` (or portal-aware) guard.
**Suggested fix:** pass a `portal`/`showFinancials` prop into `SupportTicketView` (mirroring `SupportDeskView`'s existing `portal` prop pattern) and either omit `balanceCents` from the query or conditionally render it only for `portal === "admin"`.

### 4. `CannedReplyPicker` / `lib/actions-canned-replies.ts` — **PASS**
`deleteCannedReply` (line 78) is `requireAdmin()`-only, per the plan's deliberate judgment call. `listCannedReplies`, `createCannedReply`, `updateCannedReply` all gate `requireAnyGrant(["supportTickets","liveChat"])` — not open to any authenticated user.

### 5. Task system (`lib/actions-work.ts`, `app/api/work/attachments/**`) — **PASS**
Every export in `lib/actions-work.ts` (boards, columns, tasks, checklist, comments, activity, attachment-delete — 20 exports) calls `requireGrant("tasks")` with no exceptions. Both `app/api/work/attachments/route.ts` (upload) and `app/api/work/attachments/[id]/route.ts` (download) also gate `requireGrant("tasks")`. No path-traversal risk: `WorkTask.id`/`WorkTaskAttachment.id` are `@default(cuid())` (schema lines 1916, 1968, non-user-settable), `storedName` is server-generated (`randomBytes(12).toString("hex")` + a regex-restricted extension, `/\.[A-Za-z0-9]{1,8}$/`), and the GET route never derives its filesystem path from the URL param directly — it always resolves `att.taskId`/`att.storedName` from the DB row looked up by `id`.

### 6. Structural regressions (tsc / tests) — **PASS**
- `DATABASE_URL=... npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` — clean, zero errors.
- `DATABASE_URL=... npm test` — 1342 tests, **37 failing**, matching the expected pre-existing count. Ran the two most concerning-looking failures (`HAZARD: every export of a "use server" module is authenticated...` and `no NEW call site keys anything on the caller-supplied first hop`) down to their listed offenders — `lib/actions-domains.ts`, `lib/actions-email-hosting.ts`, `lib/actions-free-minecraft.ts` (unguarded actions), `lib/fulfil-checkout.ts` (untrusted IP) — none of which this branch's diff touches for those specific functions/lines. Confirmed by running `test/auth-lockouts.test.ts` directly against `main`: identical 3 failures there too. All 37 are pre-existing and unrelated to the staff-platform work.

### 7. Full diff sanity scan — **FAIL (one out-of-scope regression, unrelated to RBAC)**
`git diff --stat main` shows 32 tracked files + a matching set of untracked new files, all plausibly in-scope for this feature (staff routes, grants, tasks, mailboxes, reddit gating, `dnd-kit` added to `package.json`) — except:

**`lib/actions-free-minecraft.ts`** (24 lines changed) has nothing to do with the staff platform and is a **functional regression**: it reverts `createFreeMinecraftServer`'s capacity check from a live-host-capacity SSH probe back to a stale `db.freeMinecraftServer.count()` over non-DELETED rows — the exact bug the deleted comment says was already found and fixed ("EVERY new signup was refused as 'at capacity' even when every existing container was asleep and the host was idle"). This looks like a stray revert accidentally picked up by one of the five parallel agents (e.g. a bad rebase/merge against an older base), not intentional work on this branch. It is not a security hole, but it silently undoes a previously-shipped fix and has no business being in this diff.
**Suggested fix:** drop this hunk from the branch (or explicitly re-apply the live-capacity-check version) before merging.

No secrets, no stray `console.log` of sensitive data, and no commented-out/disabled auth checks were found anywhere in the diff (grepped every changed/new `.ts`/`.tsx` file for `console.log(`, `if (true)`, and commented-out `requireX` calls — the only hits were legitimate prose comments).
